title: Zachary's song (Luke 1:57–80)
hook: his tongue loosed, he sings of the dayspring from on high, prayed every morning

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Ave at Nazareth: Mary's question, and her yes. Your line was full of grace.

Elizabeth gives birth to a son, and the neighbors and relatives come to rejoice with her. On the eighth day they gather for his circumcision and naming, and they've already decided: he'll be Zachary, after his father. Elizabeth says no. He shall be called John. But nobody in your family has that name, they say. So they turn to the father, still mute after all these months, and make signs. Zachary asks for a writing tablet. Everyone leans in. He writes four words: "John is his name."
screen: `THE EIGHTH DAY.` → `NOBODY IN YOUR FAMILY IS JOHN.` → `A TABLET, AND FOUR WORDS.`

segments.voice: Immediately, Luke says, his mouth is opened and his tongue loosed, and he speaks, blessing God. The silence ends with obedience: he names the child the way the angel said. And what comes out of him, filled with the Holy Ghost, is a song, called the Benedictus after its first word in Latin. In the Douay-Rheims: "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people." The first half looks back: the house of David, the prophets, the oath God swore to Abraham. Then he turns to the baby: and thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest, to go before the face of the Lord and prepare his ways. Then the image the carry comes from. The King James says: "the dayspring from on high hath visited us." The Douay says: "the Orient from on high hath visited us: To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death; to direct our feet into the way of peace." Dayspring and Orient both try to catch one Greek word, anatole: the rising of the sun, the place in the sky where light comes up. Christians hear in it Christ pictured as sunrise, coming to people sitting in the dark. So the Church sets this song at dawn: in the Liturgy of the Hours it's sung every morning at Lauds, Morning Prayer. Months of silence, and the song that broke them became the Church's morning song.
screen: `JOHN IS HIS NAME.` · `BLESSED BE THE LORD GOD OF ISRAEL.` · `ANATOLE: DAYSPRING, ORIENT, DAWN.` · `SUNG EVERY MORNING AT LAUDS.` · then, large: `TO DIRECT OUR FEET INTO THE WAY OF PEACE.`

segments.voice: Picture tomorrow's first light: the gray before dawn, then a line of gold at the window. Choose one phrase from the song to meet it, the dayspring from on high, to enlighten them that sit in darkness, or to direct our feet into the way of peace, and say it over slowly until it's yours. If you pray, it becomes a prayer; if not, let it be a way of greeting the light.
Benedictus. Latin for blessed, the first word of Zachary's song when his tongue was loosed, prayed by the Church every morning. Today's word.
Your line: the dayspring from on high. Light, coming up over people sitting in the dark. Day four hundred forty-five, done.

howItsDone: The Benedictus, Zachary's canticle, is prayed every morning at Lauds (Morning Prayer) in the Liturgy of the Hours by priests and religious, and by lay Catholics who pray the Hours.

fork.setup: you're Zachary, mute for months. your relatives want to name your son after you. they hand you a tablet. what do you write?
fork.reveal: "John is his name." and immediately his mouth was opened, and he spoke, blessing God.

original.note: Greek: rising, dawn, the east; translated dayspring (King James) and Orient (Douay) in Luke 1:78.

trapdoor: what you thought: dayspring is a nice old-fashioned word.
what it means: Christ pictured as sunrise, visiting people who sit in darkness, in the song of a man whose own silence just ended.
what a scholar hears: anatole, the rising of a heavenly light, Latin oriens, hence the Douay's Orient; the same word names the east, where the sun comes up.

chat.says: What's the Benedictus they sing at Morning Prayer?
options: Zachary's song when his voice came back, praising God for the dawn from on high.
Mary's song of praise when she visited her cousin Elizabeth.
Simeon's prayer in the Temple, asking God to let him go in peace.
chat.meaning: When Zachary wrote John is his name, his tongue was loosed and he sang the Benedictus. The Church sings it every morning at Lauds.

Benedictus.meaning: Latin: blessed, the song's first word

anatole.meaning: Greek: the rising of the sun, the dawn

Orient.meaning: the Douay's word here: the rising sun, the east

Lauds.meaning: Morning Prayer in the Liturgy of the Hours
